status_summary: The economic impact analysis (EPA-452/R-26-002, dated January 2026) for EPA's final combustion turbine standards (rule published 2026-01-15) states that EPA is no longer monetizing benefits from reducing fine particulate matter and ozone, will continue to quantify emission reductions, and will reconsider monetization once it is confident in the modeling. This goes beyond the document's call to identify co-benefits separately, since ozone and fine particulate effects are the main health endpoints of a NOx rule. EPA told the Associated Press that not monetizing does not mean valuing health impacts at zero, while environmental groups called the change unlawful. No rule on consistent and transparent consideration of costs was found, and no legal challenge specific to the change was found.

timeline.event: EPA released the combustion turbine economic impact analysis (EPA-452/R-26-002), which states that EPA is no longer monetizing PM2.5 and ozone benefits (release day per Harvard's tracker; the document is dated January 2026).
EPA published the final combustion turbine rule whose analysis applied the approach.
